chunks: From him, from Ahmad, from al-Husayn, from al-Hasan, from Zur'ah, from Sama'ah, who said:

I asked him about a man who is in an open land, and he becomes junub while he has only one garment, and he has become junub in it, and he cannot find water. He said: "He performs tayammum and prays naked, standing, indicating by gesture."

key_terms.الثَّوْبٌ: the garment or clothing he possesses
key_terms.عُرْيَانًا: in a state of nakedness, without usable covering
key_terms.فَأَجْنَبَ: he entered the state of janabah requiring ritual purification
key_terms.فَلَاةٍ: an open desert or isolated land
key_terms.يَتَيَمَّمُ: he performs tayammum as a substitute purification
key_terms.يُومِئُ إِيمَاءً: he gestures for the prayer movements instead of full bodily motions

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if he becomes junub in the wilderness, has no water, and only has one unusable garment?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for one who becomes junub in a deserted place, has no water, and possesses only a garment that has been affected by janabah. The Imam عليه السلام instructs him to perform tayammum and offer salat in a state of nakedness, standing and gesturing the movements. It highlights the flexibility of sacred law in circumstances of necessity while preserving the obligation of worship.
